<div class="cna-intro">
The methodological literature on CNA and the applied literature using CNA is rapidly growing. This page provides a mere snapshot. For a full list of CNA resources visit the [Zotero CNA Group library](https://www.zotero.org/groups/4567107/coincidence.analysis/library).
</div>

<div class="cna-sec">

## Methodological {#methodological}

The details of the state of the art of the CNA method, as implemented in the **cna** R package, are described in:

- Baumgartner, M. and Ambühl, M. (2025), [cna: An R Package for Configurational Causal Inference and Modeling](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/cna/vignettes/cna.pdf), R package vignette, The Comprehensive R Archive Network.
- Baumgartner, M. and Ambühl, M. (2020), [Causal Modeling with Multi-Value and Fuzzy-Set Coincidence Analysis](https://doi.org/10.1017/psrm.2018.45), *Political Science Research and Methods* 8, 526-542, doi: 10.1017/psrm.2018.45. Replication material at [10.7910/DVN/YIEAF1](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/YIEAF1).

**Short and informal introductions to configurational causal modeling are provided in the following papers:**

- von Thiele Schwarz, U., Sørensen, O. H., Tafvelin, S., and Roczniewska, M. (2024), [Complexity Embraced: A New Perspective on the Evaluation of Organisational Interventions](https://doi.org/10.1080/02678373.2024.2349000), *Work & Stress*, 1-7, doi: 10.1080/02678373.2024.2349000
- Whitaker, R.G., Sperber, N., Baumgartner, M., et al. (2020), [Coincidence Analysis: A New Method for Causal Inference in Implementation Science](https://implementationscience.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13012-020-01070-3), *Implementation Science* 15, 108, doi: 10.1186/s13012-020-01070-3
- Distel, B., Plattfaut, R., and Baumgartner, M. (2026), [Coincidence Analysis: An Alternative Method for Studying Causal Complexity in IS Research](https://aisel.aisnet.org/cais/vol59/iss1/46), *Communications of the Association for Information Systems* 59.

**This paper introduces CNA robustness scoring, as implemented in the frscore R package:**

- Parkkinen, V.P. and Baumgartner, M. (2023), [Robustness and Model Selection in Configurational Causal Modeling](https://doi.org/10.1177/0049124120986200), *Sociological Methods & Research* 52(1), 176-208, doi: 10.1177/0049124120986200

**This paper discusses a protocol for finding optimally obtainable consistency and coverage scores for a given data set. (The algorithms introduced in this paper are implemented in the cnaOpt R package):**

- Baumgartner, M. and Ambühl, M. (2021), [Optimizing Consistency and Coverage in Configurational Causal Modeling](https://doi.org/10.1177/0049124121995554), *Sociological Methods & Research*, doi: 10.1177/0049124121995554

**These papers uncover shortcomings of consistency and coverage and introduce two evaluation measures:**

- De Souter, L. (2024), [Evaluating Boolean Relationships in Configurational Comparative Methods](https://doi.org/10.1515/jci-2023-0014), *Journal of Causal Inference* 12(1), doi: 10.1515/jci-2023-0014
- De Souter, L. and Baumgartner, M. (2025), [New Sufficiency and Necessity Measures for Model Building with Coincidence Analysis](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13619580), *Zenodo*, doi: 10.5281/zenodo.13619580 (preprint).

**This paper investigates the impact of data imbalances (skewness) on CNA's performance:**

- Swiatczak, M. and Baumgartner, M. (2024), [Data Imbalances in Coincidence Analysis: A Simulation Study](https://doi.org/10.1177/00491241241227039), *Sociological Methods & Research*, doi: 10.1177/00491241241227039

**These papers compare CNA and QCA:**

- Swiatczak, M. (2022), [Different Algorithms, Different Models](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11135-021-01193-9), *Quality & Quantity* 56, 1913-1937
- Haesebrouck, T. and Thomann, E. (2022), [Introduction: Causation, Inferences, and Solution Types in Configurational Comparative Methods](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11135-021-01209-4), *Quality & Quantity* 56, 1867-1888

**This paper compares CNA and Logic Regression:**

- Baumgartner, M. and Falk, C. (2023), [Configurational Causal Modeling and Logic Regression](https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2021.1971510), *Multivariate Behavioral Research* 58(2), 292-310

**Older versions of the CNA method are introduced/discussed here:**

- Baumgartner, M. and Thiem, A. (2015), [Identifying Complex Causal Dependencies in Configurational Data with Coincidence Analysis](https://journal.r-project.org/articles/RJ-2015-014/RJ-2015-014.pdf), *The R Journal* 7, 176-184
- Baumgartner, M. (2013), [Detecting Causal Chains in Small-N Data](http://dx.doi.org/10.1177/1525822X12462527), *Field Methods* 25, 3-24
- Baumgartner, M. (2009), [Uncovering Deterministic Causal Structures: A Boolean Approach](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11229-008-9348-0), *Synthese* 170, 71-96
- Baumgartner, M. (2009), [Inferring Causal Complexity](http://smr.sagepub.com/cgi/content/abstract/38/1/71), *Sociological Methods & Research* 38, 71-101
